chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm with the valuation (monetary equivalent) in the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast)."

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr, the alms given at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay Zakat al-Fitr in money instead of food?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits paying Zakat al-Fitr using its monetary value (al-qimah), reflecting the scholarly view of flexibility in discharging this obligation beyond the traditional specific food items. This ruling highlights the practical adaptability of Shia jurisprudence to ensure the poor receive the equivalent benefit, a point of discussion among jurists regarding the definition of 'qimah' as either the value of the staple food or a fixed monetary amount. It underscores the underlying spirit of charity and ease in fulfilling religious duties.
